seo.title: Bathroom Survey in Finchampstead | £125 Site Visit | Install My Bathroom
seo.description: Book a £125 bathroom survey in Finchampstead. We check floor and wall construction in both the village's older buildings and the post-war homes spreading toward Wokingham and the Ridges, then give you a fixed quote.

hero.intro: Every bathroom we fit in Finchampstead starts with the same £125 site visit, whatever decade the house behind the front door was actually built in. It's the step that turns a rough idea — a layout you've sketched on the back of an envelope, a suite you've already chosen at a showroom — into a written scope and a fixed price you can plan a project against, rather than a ballpark figure that moves once work has started. Finchampstead's village core carries a number of older buildings, while the wider area — spreading out towards Wokingham and Crowthorne, and up towards Finchampstead Ridges — is largely post-war and more modern housing, built across several decades from the 1950s onward. Those two kinds of property don't behave the same way once a floor is lifted or a wall opened up, so the survey checks what's actually there rather than assuming it from the house's age or its street.

sections.heading: What the £125 survey covers
sections.body: The survey is a site visit, not a phone call or a figure worked out from photos sent over on a phone. We measure the room properly — dimensions, door swing, ceiling height, anything sloped or awkward around a chimney breast or eaves — and check what's genuinely available behind the walls and under the floor: water pressure and flow rate at source, the existing waste and supply runs, and the actual floor and wall construction once we've opened things up to look, rather than guessed at from the surface finish. We talk through your proposed layout, or the two or three options you're still weighing up, while we're still standing in the room, so anything that would change the scope — a waste move, a floor build-up issue, a fixing requirement a heavier fitting needs — gets flagged on the day rather than buried in a quote that lands a week later.

sections.heading: Surveying Finchampstead's older village-core properties
sections.body: A number of the properties we survey around Finchampstead's village core are older buildings, and that generally means solid masonry walls and, on the ground floor, a suspended timber floor rather than a solid slab. That matters directly for anyone specifying a wet room or large-format porcelain tiling, because a suspended timber floor needs checking for deflection before any tanking goes down — too much flex under a tanked wet room base or a heavy stone floor puts both the waterproofing and the tiling above it at risk. We check joist spacing, span and condition at survey, not after the floor's already been opened up mid-installation, and we check the wall construction too, since fixing a heavy wall-hung basin or a stone-topped vanity into solid masonry is a different job to fixing the same item into a modern stud partition.

sections.heading: Surveying Finchampstead's post-war and newer housing
sections.body: Further out from the centre — towards Wokingham and Crowthorne, and up towards Finchampstead Ridges — the housing is largely post-war and more modern, built across several decades from the 1950s onward, and the survey here looks quite different. Solid concrete ground floors and standard stud-wall partitions are the norm, which generally removes the suspended-floor deflection question that dominates the older village-core stock. That doesn't mean we survey any less thoroughly — we still measure actual water pressure and flow rather than assuming a newer system delivers what a rainfall shower's spec sheet promises, and we still check the substrate before specifying a wet room — but the starting point is usually more straightforward, and the survey can concentrate more on layout, services and your chosen finish than on structural remedial work.

sections.heading: Booking your Finchampstead survey
sections.body: We cover Finchampstead from our Bracknell base, along with Wokingham and Crowthorne nearby, so a survey, a follow-up visit or a snag check doesn't need a full day set aside for travel on either side. Book the £125 survey and we'll measure your room, test water pressure, check the actual floor and wall construction behind the finish, and talk through your layout options on site, then follow that up with a written scope and a fixed quote rather than a verbal estimate. If you go ahead, that fixed figure — not a number given before anyone's seen the room — is what the installation is actually programmed and costed against.

faqs.q: Does the £125 survey fee come off the final installation cost?
faqs.a: We confirm the current arrangement when you book the survey, so there's no ambiguity about how the fee applies if you go ahead with the installation.

faqs.q: Will the survey be different for an older house in Finchampstead village compared with a post-war home further out?
faqs.a: Yes, in emphasis rather than in process. In an older village-core property we look harder at floor construction — checking for deflection where ground-floor rooms have suspended timber joists — and at wall type for fixing. In the post-war and later housing that makes up most of the wider area, the construction is more standard, so the survey focuses more on confirming water pressure, service runs and your proposed layout against the room.

faqs.q: Why does floor construction matter so much for a wet room or large-format porcelain?
faqs.a: A suspended timber floor that flexes too much under load can crack tiling and break a tanking membrane's seal over time. We check joist span, spacing and condition at survey specifically so a wet room or large-format porcelain floor is only specified where the structure underneath will genuinely support it, or so the right remedial work is priced in up front.

faqs.q: Do I need to have chosen my bathroom suite before the Finchampstead survey?
faqs.a: It helps, but it isn't essential. A firm specification lets us give you an exact, fixed quote on the day; if you're still deciding, we'll survey the room's constraints and follow up once your choices are settled.

faqs.q: How far is Finchampstead from your Bracknell base?
faqs.a: Close enough that we can schedule the survey, a follow-up visit or a snag check without a full day blocked out for travel, which also helps keep the overall installation programme on schedule once work starts.

faqs.q: What should I have ready before the surveyor arrives at my Finchampstead property?
faqs.a: Access to the room itself, cleared of anything that would obstruct measuring, plus your proposed layout or specification if you've settled on one — a plan, a showroom quote or even a rough sketch all help. It's also useful to let us know roughly when you'd like work to start.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Finchampstead survey page, depicting the pre-installation measuring visit in an older village-core property. Subject and action: a tape measure laid diagonally across a section of lifted floorboards exposing joists below, a spirit level resting across the gap, and an open clipboard with a hand-marked floor plan propped against a skirting board, as if a surveyor has just checked for deflection and stepped back to note the reading. Setting and work-stage: a stripped-back ground-floor bathroom inside an older building near Finchampstead's village core, mid-renovation, one corner of flooring pulled up, exposed solid masonry visible on the far wall, late-afternoon light entering through a small cottage-style window. Composition: three-quarter angle from the doorway, the exposed joists and tape measure filling the lower-left foreground, the small window and a stack of pale limestone flooring tiles waiting to be laid receding into the background on the right. Light and materials: honed limestone flooring stacked in slabs against the wall, aged exposed masonry, a brushed nickel towel rail already fixed near the window, soft late-afternoon daylight mixing unevenly with a single bare worklight clipped near the joists. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on fixtures; no LED strip lighting anywhere in the frame; no catalog-symmetrical staging; no single uniform gold colour wash across the frame, light must fall unevenly; no hanging plants, florals or styled candles; no running water; no uniform hyper-gloss finish, stone and masonry should show natural, varied sheen and believable wear.
